function.name: lawsuit_search
function.description: Search for lawsuits related to a particular subject matter in a certain location. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

location.description: The location to perform the search in.

subject.description: The subject matter of the lawsuits.

year.description: Optional. The year in which the lawsuit was filed. Default: 2024

message.content:
**Traffic Laws in Texas – A Quick Overview** | Topic | Key Points | |-------|------------| | **Speed Limits** | • Posted limits are the law.
• On highways: 55–75 mph (often 70 mph).
• In cities: 25–35 mph.
• School zones: 20 mph (or 15 mph if a school bus is stopped). | | **Seat‑belt & Child‑Safety** | • All occupants must wear seat belts.
• Children under 8 must be in a child‑safety seat or booster.
• The “no‑seat‑belt” law applies to all vehicles. | | **Driving Under Influence (DUI)** | • Blood Alcohol Concentration (BAC) ≥ 0.08 % is illegal.
• For commercial drivers: 0.04 %.
• Penalties: fines, license suspension, possible jail time. | | **Cell‑Phone Use** | • Hand‑held use while driving is prohibited.
• Hands‑free devices are allowed. | | **Right‑of‑Way** | • Stop at red lights and stop signs.
• Yield to pedestrians in crosswalks.
• At four‑way stops, the first vehicle to arrive has the right of way. | | **School Bus** | • Stop 20 ft. on either side of a stopped school bus with flashing lights.
• Do not pass until the bus’s lights are off and the stop sign is removed. | | **Lane‑Changing & Overtaking** | • Use turn signals.
• Do not cut off other drivers. | | **Parking** | • No parking in front of driveways, fire hydrants, or on sidewalks.
• Pay attention to “no parking” signs. | | **Towing & Vehicle Registration** | • Vehicles must be registered and display valid license plates.
• Towing a vehicle requires a valid permit. | | **Insurance** | • Minimum liability coverage: $30,000 for bodily injury per person, $60,000 for bodily injury per accident, $25,000 for property damage. | | **Special Rules** | • **Texas “No‑Stop” Law**: If you’re in a city and the intersection is not controlled by a traffic signal or stop sign, you may proceed without stopping if the intersection is clear.
• **High‑way “No‑Stop” Law**: On freeways, you may proceed through an intersection without stopping if it’s safe. | ### How to Find More Detailed Information 1. **Texas Department of Transportation (TxDOT)** – Official rules, speed limits, and road safety resources. 2. **Texas Transportation Code** – The legal text governing all traffic laws. 3. **Texas Department of Public Safety (DPS)** – Licensing, insurance, and DUI enforcement details. 4. **Local County or City Ordinances** – May have additional parking or local traffic regulations. If you need specific statutes, case law, or recent updates, let me know and I can dive deeper!
